# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 85 (Bu-Vb Pc85)

**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 85
**Title (English, from literature):** Entering an inhabited area at the wrong time

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vikālagāmappavisana-sikkhāpada* constitutes the eighty-fifth rule of the *Pācittiya* section in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a monk incurs an offense requiring confession if he enters an inhabited area or village between midday and dawn (*vikāle*) without having taken leave of another monk in the monastery, unless there is an urgent exception [SuttaCentral; Vajirañāṇavarorasa 1973]. The origin story recounts that the group of six monks (*chabbaggiya*) entered a village out of hours and engaged in various types of unedifying worldly talk (*tiracchānakathā*, including topics such as kings, thieves, battles, food, and relatives) [Hüsken 1997].
Scholars have noted that this restriction was tailored specifically to monks, who generally resided outside settlements, whereas nuns resided within or near inhabited localities and were governed by distinct regulations regarding village visits [Hüsken 1997]. In monastic practice, the requirement of taking leave typically involves informing the abbot or a fellow resident before setting out for a town or village during the afternoon or evening [Vajirañāṇavarorasa 1973].
Parallels to this rule are attested across the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka lineages in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Because the origin story features the standard catalog of *tiracchānakathā*, the text shares extensive parallel passages with various discourse texts, notably the *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1), *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2), *Sandaka Sutta* (MN 76), *Tiracchānakathāsutta* (SN 56.10), and *Paṭhamakathāvatthusutta* (AN 10.69) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial textual overlap with other Vinaya rules regarding improper village visits or monastic comportment, such as *Pācittiya* 28, *Pācittiya* 46, and *Bhikkhunī Pācittiya* 51 [DharmaNexus].
